title: Enterprise & Core QBR Deck Framework (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft outlines a two-track QBR deck template: a concise Core (standard / SMB-facing) flow and a deeper Enterprise flow. The doc includes slide-by-slide titles, speaker notes, suggested data pulls, a lightweight renewal tracker layout, risk scoring rubric, and runbook actions for follow-up.

Audience:
- CSMs preparing account reviews across small, mid-market, and enterprise customers
- Solutions/AE partners joining for strategic renewals
- PM/Eng stakeholders who may present feature roadmaps or health metrics

Guiding principles (short):
- Single-page ask: each executive slide should include a clear desired outcome (renewal, expansion, escalation, pilot extension).
- Timebox: Core decks ~20 minutes + 10 Q&A. Enterprise decks 30-45 minutes with 15-20 Q&A and working session.
- Data-first: all claims should cite a metric widget or runbook query.
- Risks surfaced early (slide 3) with mitigation owners.

Deck variants overview:
1) Core Deck (Standard) – for high-velocity accounts
   - Goal: update, show value, surface friction, propose immediate next steps with a clear renewal/expansion CTA.
   - Length: 8–12 slides.
   - Attendees: CSM, optional AE.

2) Enterprise Deck – for strategic/renewal-heavy accounts
   - Goal: collaborate on roadmap and contractual outcomes, address security/compliance, negotiate multi-product packages.
   - Length: 12–20 slides + appendix.
   - Attendees: CSM, AE, Solutions Eng, Success Architect, (optional) Product/Eng lead.

Slide-by-slide: Core (8–12 slide baseline)
  1) Title + Meeting Objectives (1 slide)
     - Speaker notes: State the meeting outcomes we need: alignment on usage, decision on renewal timing, 1–2 action items.
  2) Snapshot: Account at-a-glance (1 slide)
     - Data: ARR, MRR, active seats, product modules in use, contract end date (pull from Salesforce).
     - Talk track: Quick wins since last touch; one-sentence value statement.
  3) Health & Risk Summary (1 slide)
     - Metric bullets: coverage (requests/day), latency P50/P95, error rate, support ticket trend (30/90 day).
     - Risk flag: green/amber/red + reason.
  4) Adoption highlights (1 slide)
     - Top 3 features driving value, example customer stories or quotes.
  5) Cost & Efficiency (1 slide)
     - Show token cost trend, inference latency improvements, recommended Optimize levers (batching/quantization).
  6) Roadmap / Near-term asks (1 slide)
     - Upcoming features or integrations relevant to customer; any migrations required.
  7) Renewal/Expansion proposal (1 slide)
     - Present options with clear ask: renew + seat increase, add Dedicated pool, or pilot Private.
  8) Risks & Mitigations + Owner (1 slide)
     - Actionable plan with owners and target dates.
  9) Appendix / Data pulls (optional)
     - Queries and sources for the metrics shown.

Slide-by-slide: Enterprise (expanded)
  1) Title + Strategic Objectives (1)
  2) Executive Summary (1) – 3 bullets: impact, ask, timeline
  3) Account Landscape & Org Map (1) – stakeholder names + renewal owner
  4) Contract & Commit History (1) – past 12–24 months, uplift events
  5) Usage & Performance Deep-dive (2) – custom charts: tokens by endpoint, P99 latency, tail latency incidents
  6) Security & Compliance Posture (1) – certs, audit status, open items
  7) Business Impact Narratives (1) – two short case vignettes inside the customer org
  8) Cost Optimization Opportunities (1) – exact suggestions and expected $/month savings
  9) Roadmap / Co-investment Options (1–2) – feature prioritization + potential pilot timelines
 10) Renewal & Commercial Options (1) – licensing, committed capacity, price anchors
 11) Negotiation Playbook (1) – concessions we can offer and limits (SLA credits, migration support)
 12) Closing: Asks, Decision Timeline, Success Criteria (1)
  13) Appendix: telemetry queries, SRE incident timeline, audit log extracts (separate slides)

Speaker notes style guide (short):
- Exec slide: lead with impact ("We reduced inference cost by 28% for the reports team, resulting in a 5% margin improvement")
- Technical slide: call out what changed, who owns follow-up, and a one-line customer-facing explanation
- Ask slide: offer 2 options (preferred + fall-back) with price/commitment delta

Renewal tracker (lightweight schema described):
- Row fields to populate (suggested): customer_name | ARR_band | contract_end | renewal_owner | renewal_stage | next_meeting | last_touch | risk_score | recommended_action | notes
- Example row text: "Acme Corp | $250k | 2026-08-15 | Lina R. | Negotiation | 2026-03-10 | 2026-02-28 | 6/10 | propose 10% seat bump + 6mo pilot of Dedicated | needs security SOC2 doc"
- Recommended use: maintain a Google Sheet with filters for contract_end in next 90/180/365 days; link a slide that snapshots the high-risk accounts for this quarter.

Risk scoring rubric (quick):
- 1–3: Low (renewal likely)
- 4–6: Medium (needs touchpoints and remediation)
- 7–10: High (exec level intervention; legal/compliance blockers)
- Inputs: product usage trend, number of P1/P2 incidents, payment history, feature fit, net promoter signal from support survey.

Playbook actions (post QBR) – runbook checklist
- Within 24 hours: send recap email with slides + single page TL;DR + 3 action owners (owner: CSM)
- Day 3–5: Confirm legal/commercial asks and handoff to AE/sales (owner: AE)
- Week 2: Kick off technical work for any pilot migrations (owner: Solutions Eng)
- Ongoing: add renewal milestone to internal shared calendar and update Salesforce/linear ticket.

Data sources & placeholder queries (notes):
- Telemetry: metrics from Observability Console (latency, errors) – include screenshot links in the appendix.
- Billing: query billing export for monthly token spend by endpoint (used for Cost & Efficiency slide).
- Support: export ticket counts from Zendesk (30/90 day trends).

Email & Slack templates (short snippets):
- Email subject (exec): "[Acme] QBR recap + renewal options — decision requested by 2026-05-01"
- Slack: "@solutions-eng FYI: we proposed 6mo Dedicated pilot for Acme — can you confirm SE availability in May?"

Appendix (templates to copy into decks):
- Slide template: Title + 2-column content (left: metric chart; right: short narrative + ask)
- Executive one-pager template: 1/2 page impact summary + 3 bullets (ask, rationale, timeline)

Open questions / TODOs for this draft:
- Need sample data pulls for two canonical account archetypes (platform-heavy vs product-API). Lina to provide examples by 2025-11-22.
- Confirm legal concessions matrix for enterprise renewals (legal + finance input).
- Decide whether to include a live salesforce widget in the slide export or static screenshot (design ops input).

Notes for CSMs (quick tips):
- Bring a forward-looking metric (e.g., forecasted cost efficiency with Optimize) not just historical data.
- When discussing performance, translate technical improvement into developer/product outcomes (faster response = higher conversions).
- For enterprise execs: lead with business outcomes and retention levers, save the technical deep dive for a breakout session.

Changelog (draft history):
- 2025-11-12: initial outline (A. Patel)
- 2025-11-18: added renewal tracker schema + risk rubric (Liam O'C)
- 2026-01-10: inserted enterprise negotiation playbook (Rhea S.)
- 2026-02-28: updated speaker notes & data source pointers (A. Patel)

Attachments to create for final pack (next steps):
- Google Slides master: Core template + Enterprise template (CS deck master)
- Google Sheet: Renewal tracker with filters and dashboard
- One-pager: Exec TL;DR PDF export for email attachment

Contact notes: reach out to product@redwood.ai for roadmap syncs and billing@redwood.ai for spend validation.

End of draft.
